card1.title: Why do cylindrical pipes and vessels always rupture longitudinally?
card1.description: In thin-walled cylindrical shells, circumferential (hoop) stress is exactly twice the longitudinal stress. When internal pressure exceeds limits, the vessel invariably bursts along its length rather than circumference!

card2.title: 98% particulate separation achieved with zero moving parts!
card2.description: Industrial hydrocyclones transform fluid pressure into extreme rotational velocity, generating centrifugal accelerations thousands of times greater than gravity to separate dense solids within milliseconds.

card3.title: Cavitation: when microscopic vapor bubbles pit hardened steel!
card3.description: When local pressure drops below saturation vapor pressure, microbubbles form and violently collapse upon entering higher pressure zones. The resulting micro-jets exceed 1,000 atmospheres, eroding titanium impellers.

card4.title: Regime transitions and 40% thermal conductivity surges via nanofluids
card4.description: Re ≈ 2300 marks the onset of turbulent flow. Suspending less than 1% volumetric concentration of metallic oxide nanoparticles can elevate heat exchanger transfer coefficients by up to 40% with minimal viscosity penalty.
card4.formula: Re = (ρ × v × D) / μ | k_nano > 1.4 × k_base
